newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas slips on fresh supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas slips on fresh supplies.

text.p: Ample supplies and weak demand depressed gasoline prices in Singapore on Monday, traders said.

State-owned Saudi Aramco emerged with its usual quarterly tender, offering 32,000 to 35,000 tonnes of 98-octane unleaded reformate lifting July 26-28 from Jubail on the Red Sea, industry sources said.
The tender closes on July 8, they said.
Traders viewd the announcement as bearish.
"There is no outlet except Taiwan," a trader said. "But the cargo is even too prompt for that."
Most traders were out of the market, citing Taiwan's buy tender for August, closing on July 9 as the dampener of spot trade.
"The market is long, demand is thin and everybody again is waiting for Taiwan," a trader with a major oil company said.
Only one bid was heard for 97-octane unleaded cargo, at $23.60 per barrel fob Singapore lifting August 2-6.
Whilst waiting for the Taiwan tender to close, the market was rife with rumours of two 95-octane leaded cargoes sold to state-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex).
The prompt cargoes were said sold by a Singapore and Japanese trader at $2.75 over Singapore naphtha quotes fob Vietnam's.
But the Singapore trader and Petrolimex denied the deals.
Petrolimex said earlier it was still seeking two more cargoes as it could not buy all its requirments in its third quarter tender due to the lack of offers.

Petrolimex last week bought one July and September and two August delivery cargoes of 18,000-tonne cargoes of 83-octane leaded gasoline of Russian origin at 70-cents per barrel over Singapore spot naphtha quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City, Danang or Hongai.
Naphtha swaps edged down marginally to $20.50/20.65 per barrel.
The amply supplied naphtha saw fresh supplies from India putting pressure on on prompt levels, traders said.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has three outstanding tenders, offering 79,000-tonnes lifting in July.
Two tenders close on July 10, selling 27,000 tonnes of HAN lifting July 24-26 from Madras on the east coast and 25,000-tonnes of LAN from Bombay, on the west coast.
The third which closes July 17, is offering HAN from Cochin on the west coast between July 27-29.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
